Scene: Strait of Hormuz, danger of a maritime bottleneck. LEFT foreground: terrified white round-headed Stick ship captain in simple navy uniform and a plain WHITE peaked captain cap with black visor and a gold band, without an anchor or badge. Huge wide eyes, eyebrows arched, open alarmed mouth, blue sweat drops, looking RIGHT toward the tanker. His face occupies the left third below the calm top strip. CENTRE-RIGHT: one very large recognizable oil tanker seen in a dramatic elevated three-quarter view with its bow pointing toward the lower right foreground, broad red/orange hull, dark deck with oil pipes and white superstructure. It is squeezing through a visually VERY NARROW deep-blue water corridor between two looming dark simplified coastlines. This is a stylized geographic compression of the Iran/Oman choke point, no labels. ONE large black spherical horned naval mine with a strong RED glow floats directly in front of the tanker's bow, clearly separate and close enough to block its route. A THIN YELLOW navigation route line runs through the narrow gap beside/under the tanker and toward the mine. Do not turn the route into text. Strong navy water, black coastlines, warm tanker and red mine. Keep captain and tanker equally crisp; one clear face, one tanker, one mine. TOP strip completely calm and empty.
